title: bug: PowerShell 5.1 seats fail closed with MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED in every Git project when the Windows temp path contains a space
description:
Filed by the architect at QA's request (qa-952969be, chan-845e71c6 msg-2514b792). task-76ae5c47 uses a space-free temp name and keeps this bug out of its scope. The bug has existed since 447281cf (task-c4cd6dce, agent Git-write guard).

Failure (measured 2026-10-30, Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.9711):
- Initialize-MoeAgentGitGuard (scripts/moe-agent.ps1 ~L5986) runs `$program | & node - $projectPath ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath())`. GetTempPath() always ends in a backslash.
- PS 5.1 passes native arguments with legacy quoting. It wraps an argument that contains a space in double quotes and does not double its trailing backslash, so node's argv parser reads the final `\"` as a literal quote. Probe: the argument 'C:\x y\' arrives as 'C:\x y"'.
- The guard program's fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(temp, 'moe-git-guard-')) then fails, because a quote is not legal in a Windows path. The program prints MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED and exits 1, and the wrapper throws before the CLI starts.

Impact:
- Whenever GetTempPath() contains a space, every PS 5.1 seat in a Git project refuses to launch. That covers every CLI (claude, codex, gemini, grok, custom) and every role, notification-only sessions included. In a non-Git project the guard exits before it reaches the temp path.
- GetTempPath() reads TMP, then TEMP, then USERPROFILE. Two examples take every seat on that machine down: a TMP/TEMP override such as 'D:\My Temp', and a profile folder such as 'C:\Users\First Last' when TEMP does not hold its 8.3 short form. The JetBrains plugin runs native Windows seats under PS 5.1.
- The error names neither the space nor the temp path.
- Workaround until this is fixed: point TMP and TEMP at a space-free directory for the IDE or launcher process.
- Not affected: bash (moe-agent.sh, WSL mode included) passes argv verbatim. PS 7.3+ is expected to escape the trailing backslash (not measured).

Fix direction. This is a candidate; the planner may choose another that meets the DoD.
- Pass `([IO.Path]::GetTempPath() + '.')`. Probe: node receives 'C:\x y\.', and path.join gives 'C:\x y\moe-git-guard-'. A drive-root temp stays absolute: 'C:\' + '.' gives 'C:\moe-git-guard-'. TrimEnd('\') would instead leave the drive-relative 'C:'.
- Keep the embedded node program byte-identical with moe-agent.sh's MOE_GIT_GUARD_JS heredoc. Leave moe-agent.sh untouched, and every launch line that codexDescriptor.ts pins.
- Check the other native-command calls in moe-agent.ps1 for the same pattern: an argument that can contain a space and end in a backslash, such as a -Project path given with a trailing backslash. Fix one here only when it is the same one-token change. Otherwise report it on this row and do not widen the task.

Lane and overlap:
- This row edits scripts/moe-agent.ps1 and scripts/tests/agent-git-guard.test.mjs, so it joins the serialized wrapper lane.
- As a safe default, it depends on task-76ae5c47, the current ps1 tail. The governor owns the final slot.
- task-76ae5c47 wraps the same ~L5986 line in an encoding try/finally. Whichever row lands second keeps the other's change.
- If task-76ae5c47 has landed, reuse its test's TMP/TEMP plumbing: delete every TMP/TEMP key from the fixture env, in any letter case, then set both.
definitionOfDone: On native Windows PowerShell 5.1, a seat in a Git project whose [IO.Path]::GetTempPath() contains a space launches its guarded CLI. In the test, TMP and TEMP point to a fixture directory whose name contains a space. The seat's core.hooksPath resolves under that directory, and no moe-git-guard- entry remains there after exit. A new case in scripts/tests/agent-git-guard.test.mjs proves it: on the unfixed parent it fails with 'CLI did not run' and MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED, and after the fix it passes. Under Linux bash the same case passes with a spaced TMPDIR.

The embedded guard program stays byte-identical with scripts/moe-agent.sh's MOE_GIT_GUARD_JS heredoc. scripts/moe-agent.sh and every launch line that codexDescriptor.ts pins are unchanged. Every existing guard case still passes unchanged, the fail-closed modes included.

These all pass: the guard suite on Linux bash and on native Windows PS 5.1 (0 skipped on Windows), the prompt-cache and usage launcher harnesses, postflight-safe bash and powershell, and parity-check. The completion summary gives each count beside the parent's.

implementationPlan.description:
Test first (RED). Use test-driven-development. Read these first: mem:task-task-408a0ac1524b4ab4a6418dd741b53d8d-handoff, mem:task-task-76ae5c472f6a4651a45478b1893e07dc-handoff, mem:gotcha-agent-git-guard-runtime-config, and this row's planner comment (comment-29bee9da).

In scripts/tests/agent-git-guard.test.mjs, add ONE case.
- Seat: cli 'custom', headless (interactive false), commitHooks false, status REVIEW, mode 'spaced-temp'. This is the seat the planner measured RED.
- Title: include 'spaced temp', so that `--test-name-pattern 'spaced temp'` selects exactly this case.

Reuse what task-76ae5c47 (dependsOn, lands first) added for its two 'non-ascii-temp' cases: the optional 5th matrix element (mode), the TMP/TEMP env plumbing, and its extra assertions. Re-read the file at start_step and mirror whatever shape it actually landed.
- Only the directory name differs: path.join(root, 'My Temp'), ASCII with a space. Create it before launch, inside the fixture root that t.after removes.
- If that plumbing is inline under mode === 'non-ascii-temp', key the directory name by mode, e.g. { 'non-ascii-temp': 'témp', 'spaced-temp': 'My Temp' }. The non-ascii-temp cases must keep the same directory, env and assertions.
- Its CP 850 driver and stub pins stay on its own mode. This case uses the default stub and driver.

Env:
- Windows: delete every f.env key matching /^(TMP|TEMP)$/i, then set TMP and TEMP to the directory. GetTempPath reads TMP first, and a spread process.env is no longer case-insensitive.
- Linux: set TMPDIR to the directory.

Assertions:
- Every matrix assertion.
- core.hooksPath (observed.hooks) resolves under the directory: compare path.resolve'd strings, case-insensitively on Windows.
- After exit, a recursive walk of the directory finds no entry whose name starts with moe-git-guard-.

RED message:
- The shared check's `codes=` lists the MOE_ codes found in r.stdout only, but the wrapper's refusal goes to stderr (measured: codes=null).
- So for this case only, before the shared check, assert fs.existsSync(f.result) with the message `CLI did not run: exit=${r.status}; codes=${(r.stdout + r.stderr).match(/MOE_[A-Z_]+/g)}`. The RED then names both 'CLI did not run' and MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED, as the DoD requires.
- Leave the shared check and every other case unchanged. If 76ae5c47 already widened the shared check, reuse it.

RED proof on native Windows (recipe in step 3):
- Take a snapshot of the parent (HEAD at start, unfixed ps1) with only this test file overlaid.
- Run node.exe --test on the three gate files.
- Expect exactly one failure: this case, failing with 'CLI did not run' and MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED. Keep that line.
- The per-file counts, minus this case, are the parent's Windows counts for the summary.
- On Linux the case passes before and after the fix. The planner measured all 24 existing cases passing under a spaced TMPDIR on HEAD (51 s).
- Never put scratch copies inside the checkout.

Error handling: everything the case creates stays inside the fixture root, and no env change leaks into other cases, because f.env is per fixture.

Fix scripts/moe-agent.ps1, function Initialize-MoeAgentGitGuard. In the line that pipes the embedded program into `& node - $projectPath ...`, change the single token `([IO.Path]::GetTempPath())` to `([IO.Path]::GetTempPath() + '.')`. Nothing else in the runtime changes.

Keep exactly as landed:
- task-76ae5c47's [Console]::OutputEncoding save/set/restore around that line (QA has said it will check this at review);
- the MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED throw on a nonzero exit;
- the env.json read.

Add one short ASCII comment above the line saying why:
- PS 5.1 wraps a native argument that contains a space in double quotes but does not double its trailing backslash, so node read 'C:\x y\' as 'C:\x y"' and mkdtemp failed closed.
- GetTempPath() always ends in a separator, so '.' names the same directory.
- TrimEnd('\') would turn a drive root into the drive-relative 'C:'.

Out of scope, leave untouched:
- the embedded program, which is byte-identical with moe-agent.sh's MOE_GIT_GUARD_JS heredoc;
- $projectPath: the trailing-backslash -Project finding is reported on this row (comment-29bee9da), not fixed here;
- Invoke-MoeGuardedCommand and Remove-MoeAgentGitGuard, the span the launcher harnesses cut;
- every launch line, which codexDescriptor.ts pins;
- scripts/moe-agent.sh: its working tree holds a peer's uncommitted edits, so never stage, revert or overlay it.

Use the Edit tool only, so the UTF-8 BOM and LF line endings survive.

Planner measurements on PS 5.1.26100.9711:
- Node receives 'C:\…\x y\.' and path.join gives 'C:\…\x y\moe-git-guard-'.
- 'C:\' + '.' joins to 'C:\moe-git-guard-'.
- '\\srv\share\x y\' + '.' stays UNC.
- With only this change, all 24 existing guard cases pass under a spaced TMP/TEMP (134 s).
- PS 7.3+ passes 'C:\x y\.' through intact as well.

Error handling: a node failure still throws MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED and never launches unguarded.

Then re-run the step 1 case under native Windows node. It must pass, with no moe-git-guard- entry left in the spaced directory.

Verification gate. Run it once, fresh, after steps 1-2. Its output is the complete_task evidence.

Where not to run it:
- Never in the shared tree: the guard suite executes scripts/moe-agent.sh, whose working tree holds a peer's uncommitted bytes.
- Never run npm build, test or install there either (GLOBAL rail).

Linux:
- Make a fresh mktemp dir $L and run `git archive HEAD | tar -x -C $L`.
- Overlay exactly the two owned files, and `cmp` each one against the worktree.
- From $L, run exactly:
`unset ${!MOE_@} ${!CLAUDE_@} ${!FAKE_@}; node --test scripts/tests/agent-git-guard.test.mjs scripts/tests/prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs scripts/tests/usage-launcher.test.mjs && node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh`
- Submit that run's command, exitCode and outputTail.
- For the parent's Linux counts, run the same node --test on a `git archive` snapshot of the parent.

Native Windows is also required. No PowerShell skip counts as a pass, and Linux pwsh never substitutes for PS 5.1.
- Make the snapshot on a Windows drive outside the repo, e.g. mktemp -d under /mnt/c/Users/<user>/AppData/Local/Temp, with the same overlay and cmp. Never use a \\wsl$ cwd.
- Check that `cmd.exe /d /c "set MOE"` prints 'not defined'.
- From that dir (via `cmd.exe /d /c "cd /d <dir> && ..."` or a powershell.exe -File runner), run `"C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe" --test scripts/tests/agent-git-guard.test.mjs scripts/tests/prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs scripts/tests/usage-launcher.test.mjs`. It must show 0 failed and 0 skipped. The planner's guard-file run took 134 s.
- Then, alone and not in parallel with that run, run `"C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe" scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell`. It must show failureClass NONE and lastScenario Z (about 26 min, against a 30-min cap).
- Delete both snapshots afterwards, checking each path prefix first.

The completion summary gives each count beside the parent's:
- guard: the parent's count + 1, with 0 skipped on both platforms;
- each launcher harness: the parent's count, 0 failed (Linux skips only the PS-only cases);
- postflight-safe bash and powershell: exit 0, NONE/Z;
- parity-check: PASS.
Also include the step 1 RED line, both Windows wall-clock times, and the step 4 twin check.

If any run is red, fix it and re-run the whole gate. Never cite a partial run.

Final adversarial self-review, one pass, scoped to this task's own diff. The epic is a standing bug bucket, so there is no whole-epic sweep.

Runtime diff:
- `git diff -- scripts/moe-agent.ps1` shows only the one token plus the comment.
- 76ae5c47's encoding try/finally is intact.
- The BOM is intact (first bytes ef bb bf), and line endings are still LF.

Twin check (parity-check does not cover it):
- Write a small node script in a scratch dir outside the checkout.
- Cut the text between `    $program = @'\n` and `\n'@\n` in moe-agent.ps1.
- Cut the text between `<<'MOE_GIT_GUARD_JS'\n` and `\nMOE_GIT_GUARD_JS\n` in `git show HEAD:scripts/moe-agent.sh`.
- Each anchor must occur exactly once, and the two strings must be equal. The planner measured 4453 equal chars on HEAD.

Other invariants:
- This task changed no byte of scripts/moe-agent.sh: it is not in modifiedFiles, and `git diff HEAD -- scripts/moe-agent.sh` shows only the peer hunks that were there at start.
- `grep -cF` each of the three codexDescriptor.ts PowerShell literals (L29, L31, L462) in moe-agent.ps1: each must still count 1.

Questions to answer:
- Can '.' ever name a different directory? Only if GetTempPath() lacked its trailing separator, which .NET guarantees. A drive root and a UNC path stay absolute (measured).
- Does the new case fail without the fix, with both strings in the RED message (step 1)? Does it pass on Linux with a spaced TMPDIR?
- Are every other case's assertions, stubs and drivers byte-identical?
- Can TMP/TEMP keys collide by case?
- Is net growth well under 400 LOC?

Restate this row's audit finding in the completion summary: the trailing-backslash -Project issue, reported and not fixed.

Fix any finding and re-run the step 3 gate before complete_task. Hand off to QA; never approve your own work.

comments.author: architect-bd1eb82d
comments.content:
Planner measurements and native-argument audit. Measured by architect-bd1eb82d on 2026-10-30 at HEAD 864d787c, Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.9711, in snapshots outside the checkout.

1. RED. The case 'PS5.1 custom headless plumbing completion', run with TMP/TEMP set to '…\tmp x y', fails in 3 s with 'CLI did not run: exit=1; codes=null'.
- stderr: 'MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED: refusing to launch an unprotected CLI', then the throw at moe-agent.ps1:5987.
- codes= is null because the shared check scans r.stdout only.

2. Fix. Changing only `([IO.Path]::GetTempPath() + '.')` on the node call line makes all 24 existing PS 5.1 guard cases pass under that spaced TMP/TEMP, in 134 s: every CLI, interactive and headless, plus the fail-closed and concurrent cases.
- Node receives 'C:\…\x y\.' and path.join gives '…\x y\moe-git-guard-'.
- 'C:\' + '.' gives 'C:\moe-git-guard-'.
- '\\srv\share\x y\' + '.' stays UNC.

3. Linux. All 24 cases pass unchanged with a spaced TMPDIR, in 51 s. moe-agent.sh needs no edit.

4. Audit of the other native calls.
- No other temp consumer passes a path that ends in a separator to a native command:
  - L2629, L4100 and L4658 use Join-Path;
  - L4609 only compares with StartsWith;
  - every $env:TEMP use is a Join-Path to a file;
  - GetTempFileName returns a file path.
- Not fixed here, because it is not the same one-token change: Resolve-Path (L373) keeps a trailing backslash. So `-Project 'C:\x y\'` reaches every native call that passes $projectPath:
  - the guard's node call;
  - Get-MoeGitTop's `& git -C $projectPath` (L2529-2545);
  - the codex `-C "$projectPath"` launch lines that codexDescriptor.ts pins.
- Measured: `& git -C 'C:\…\x y\' rev-parse --show-prefix` fails with "fatal: cannot change to 'C:\…\x y" rev-parse --show-prefix': Invalid argument". The trailing \" swallows every later argument.
- The fix belongs at L373 (trim a trailing separator that is not a root), and 3ad573a7 is rewriting that line.
- JetBrains passes project.basePath, which has no trailing separator, so only hand-typed launches are exposed.
- This is a candidate follow-up row. Filing it is the governor's call.

comments.author: architect-b58e1112

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Chosen: append '.' to GetTempPath() at the one node call. It is one token, needs no twin change, and the measured result is green across all 24 existing PS 5.1 cases under a spaced TEMP.

Rejected:
- TrimEnd('\'): a drive root becomes the drive-relative 'C:'.
- Appending '\' to double the backslash: it works under legacy quoting, but every space-free temp then carries a doubled separator in argv, which is less obvious.
- Passing the temp root via an env var: the embedded node program reads process.argv.slice(-2) and must stay byte-identical with the sh heredoc.
- A generic native-argument escaping helper: a much wider change, and PS 7.3+ already escapes correctly.
- Start-Process with a hand-built ArgumentList: it loses the pipeline stdin that carries the program.
- Normalizing $projectPath at L373: that is a separate bug, not this token. 3ad573a7 is rewriting that line, so the finding is reported on the row (comment-29bee9da).
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Measured 2026-10-30 at HEAD 864d787c, PS 5.1.26100.9711:
- Legacy native quoting delivers 'C:\x y\' to node as 'C:\x y"'. A trailing \" also swallows every later argument into the same argv element.
- With + '.', node gets 'C:\x y\.' and path.join gives 'C:\x y\moe-git-guard-'.
- Resolve-Path keeps a trailing backslash ('C:\x y\' stays 'C:\x y\', with -Path or -LiteralPath).

Guard case behavior:
- Unfixed, the custom headless plumbing case under TMP/TEMP '...\tmp x y' fails in 3 s with 'CLI did not run: exit=1; codes=null'.
- stderr: node's 'MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED: refusing to launch an unprotected CLI', then the PS throw at ps1:5987.
- Fixed, the 24 existing cases pass in 134 s.
- Linux: 24/24 pass unchanged with a spaced TMPDIR (51 s). Bash passes argv verbatim, and its guard root lives under mktemp -d.

Test-harness facts:
- The shared 'CLI did not run' message lists MOE_ codes from stdout only.
- parity-check does not compare the embedded program twins. The planner's node cut-and-compare found them equal (4453 chars).
- The launcher harnesses cut ps1 from 'function Invoke-MoeGuardedCommand {' to 'function Remove-MoeAgentGitGuard', below the fix.
- codexDescriptor.ts pins only the Invoke-MoeGuardedCommand launch literals.
planningNotes.risks:
- 76ae5c47 lands first and changes the same test file and the ps1 line, so re-read both at start_step. Keep its encoding try/finally (QA said it will check), and mirror its matrix mechanism instead of inventing a second one.
- The RED message must contain both 'CLI did not run' and MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED. The refusal goes to stderr, so the case-specific pre-check must scan stdout and stderr.
- On Windows, f.env may hold TMP/TEMP in another letter case: delete case-insensitively before setting.
- Shared checkout: scripts/moe-agent.sh holds a peer's uncommitted bytes, so run every gate from snapshots, and no npm in packages (GLOBAL rail).
- postflight-safe powershell takes about 26 min against a 30-min cap. Run it alone.
- moe-agent.ps1 must keep its BOM: use the Edit tool.
- The trailing-backslash -Project bug stays out of scope. Restate it in the summary; do not widen the task.
